feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 10 (450.6, best) is the strongest evidence: its oval finished 20 of 20 and its s-bend progress was 0.61. Iteration 8 (417.9, radius 0.040 m and track 0.10 m at body 0.14 m) showed that radius helped the s-bend (0.655) but cost oval stability (19 of 20). Iteration 9 (mass 0.5 kg, 382.3) showed that a lighter robot lost oval finishes (18 of 20) and s-bend progress (0.521). Footprint 0.016 m collapsed the oval (iteration 6) and 0.008 m dropped s-bend progress to 0.32 (iteration 7), so 0.012 m stays. Widening the sensor span raised oscillation (iteration 2). The slalom has stayed at 0.16 to 0.20 progress across iterations 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10, so sensing, track and mass have not moved it. For a further iteration, if the slalom passes 0.20 with s-bend at or above 0.6, the body and radius direction is working; if the oval drops below 18 finishes or oscillation exceeds about 0.35, return to the iteration 10 values. If the slalom stays at 0.16 to 0.20, treat it as a controller limit rather than a geometry limit.
requested_changes: If the slalom progress passes 0.20 and s-bend progress holds at or above 0.6 with body_length 0.10 m, try wheel_radius 0.045 m with wheel_track 0.10 m. Iteration 8 showed that radius raised s-bend progress (0.486 to 0.655), and the oval should hold at 18 or more finishes.

If the oval falls below 18 of 20 or steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.35 with body_length 0.10 m, return body_length to 0.14 m and mass to 0.6 kg, the iteration 8 values. Iteration 9 showed that lighter mass also reduced oval finishes, so do not combine mass changes with this.

If the slalom stays at 0.16 to 0.20 with max_error near 0.06 (iterations 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 and 10), stop changing sensing, track, radius or mass. Keep the best-supported geometry and pass the slalom to the Integrator as a controller reaction-time issue.
